questions.question: Von Neumann architecture is based on —
questions.answer:
**Correct answer: A) SISD.**

The classic stored-program Von Neumann machine has one instruction stream and one data stream.

questions.question: Example for zero address instructions is —
questions.answer:
**Correct answer: A) push.**

Zero-address instructions operate on the top of a stack, so they need no explicit memory/register address.

questions.question: What is the full form of TLB?
questions.answer:
**Correct answer: B) Translation Look-aside Buffer.**

A TLB caches recent virtual-to-physical page translations.

questions.question: What is Page Map Table?

options.text: It maps the virtual addresses to physical addresses
It maps physical addresses to virtual addresses
It maps the virtual addresses to Logical addresses

questions.answer:
**Correct answer: A.**

A page map/page table translates virtual page numbers into physical frame numbers.

questions.question: The result of `MOV AL, 65` is to store —
questions.answer:
**Correct answer: D) 0100 0001 in AL.**

Decimal 65 is `41H`, which is binary `0100 0001`.
questions.sourceNote: Handwritten tick on the scan confirms option D; no official key was supplied.

questions.question: Which of the following is page fault?

options.text: Page fault occurs when a program accesses a page of another program
Page fault occurs when a program accesses a page in main memory
Page fault occurs when there is an error in particular page
Page fault occurs when a program accesses a page which is not present in main memory

questions.answer:
**Correct answer: D.**

A page fault traps to the OS when the referenced page is valid but not resident in main memory.

questions.question: Which of the following are the two main components of the CPU?
questions.answer:
**Correct answer: C) CU and ALU.**

The control unit directs operations; the arithmetic/logic unit executes them. Registers are internal storage.

questions.question: The term that provides simultaneous data processing tasks are —
questions.answer:
**Correct answer: A) parallel processing.**

Parallel processing executes multiple operations concurrently. Vector/array processing are more specific forms.

questions.question: A `16 × 8` organisation of memory cells can store upto —
questions.answer:
**Correct answer: D) 128 bits.**

`16 × 8 = 128` cells/bits in the usual 16 words × 8 bits per word interpretation.

questions.question: A processor can access a memory location by 32 bits. Then find the total memory size if all memory locations are available to the processor.
questions.answer:
**Correct answer: A) 4 GB.**

A 32-bit address selects `2^32` byte-addressed locations = 4 GiB.

questions.question: Data transfer from Cache Memory to Processor is —
questions.answer:
**Correct answer per the scan annotation: B) Block by Block.**

The handwritten mark selects B. In many textbooks, cache-to-CPU transfers are word-by-word while main-memory-to-cache transfers are block-by-block, so this item is architecture-convention dependent.
questions.sourceNote: The scan’s handwritten tick selects B. A standard alternative convention would make A correct for cache-to-processor word transfers; no official key exists.

questions.question: In which of the following term the performance of cache memory is measured?
questions.answer:
**Correct answer: B) Hit ratio.**

Hit ratio = cache hits / total accesses; miss ratio and average access time are derived from it.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT involved in the case of a memory write operation?
questions.answer:
**Correct answer: D) PC.**

MAR holds the address and MDR the data; the data bus carries it. The program counter is not part of the memory write data path.

questions.question: Which of the following memory unit communicates directly with the CPU?
questions.answer:
**Correct answer: B) Main memory.**

The CPU addresses main memory directly; auxiliary/secondary storage is reached through I/O controllers.

questions.question: A computer system supports `2^46` logical addresses and `2^11` addresses per page. How many pages can be represented in secondary memory (virtual memory address space)?
questions.answer:
**Correct answer: B) 2^35.**

Number of pages = `2^46 / 2^11 = 2^35`.
questions.sourceNote: OCR flattened `2^35` to `235`; restored from the page crop.

questions.question:
a) Draw the Von Neumann basic structure and mark all its components.
b) Draw and explain the BUS architecture of a digital computer.

subparts.label: a
subparts.text: Draw the Von Neumann basic structure and mark all its components.

subparts.label: b
subparts.text: Draw and explain the BUS architecture of a digital computer.

questions.answer:
**a)** A Von Neumann machine has CPU (CU + ALU + registers), main memory, input, output, and shared address/data/control buses. Instructions and data share the same memory.

**b)** System buses: address bus carries location, data bus carries words, control bus carries read/write/clock/interrupt signals. All devices attach to these shared lines.

questions.question:
a) Explain the basic instruction cycle with appropriate diagram.
b) Write the Zero address instructions to evaluate `X = (A+B) * (C+D)`.

subparts.label: a
subparts.text: Explain the basic instruction cycle with appropriate diagram.

subparts.label: b
subparts.text: Write the Zero address instructions to evaluate `X = (A+B) * (C+D)`.

questions.answer:
**a)** Fetch → decode → fetch operands → execute → store result → update PC, repeated under clock control.

**b)**
```text
PUSH A; PUSH B; ADD
PUSH C; PUSH D; ADD
MUL
POP X
```

questions.question:
a) Write the difference between Minimum Mode and Maximum Mode in 8086 Microprocessor.
b) Explain with example any four addressing modes available in 8086 microprocessors.

subparts.label: a
subparts.text: Write the difference between Minimum Mode and Maximum Mode in 8086 Microprocessor.

subparts.label: b
subparts.text: Explain with example any four addressing modes available in 8086 microprocessors.

questions.answer:
**a)** Minimum mode is a single-processor system where 8086 generates control signals directly; maximum mode supports multiprocessor/coprocessor systems and uses an 8288 bus controller.

**b)** Immediate `MOV AX,5`; register `MOV AX,BX`; direct `MOV AX,[1234H]`; register indirect `MOV AX,[BX]`; also indexed/based and based-indexed modes.

questions.question:
a) Write the different cache mapping techniques and explain it.
b) A typical computer system cache memory access time is 8 ns and its main memory access time is 80 ns. If hit ratio is 90%, what is the average memory access time?

subparts.label: a
subparts.text: Write the different cache mapping techniques and explain it.

subparts.label: b
subparts.text: A typical computer system cache memory access time is 8 ns and its main memory access time is 80 ns. If hit ratio is 90%, what is the average memory access time?

questions.answer:
**a)** Direct mapping: one fixed cache line per memory block. Fully associative: any block in any line. Set-associative: a block maps to a set and can occupy any way in it.

**b)** With concurrent lookup: `0.9×8 + 0.1×80 = 15.2 ns`. If the miss penalty is added after the cache lookup: `8 + 0.1×80 = 16 ns`. State the convention used.

questions.question:
a) Write the difference between CISC & RISC Architecture.
b) Write short notes on any one: i) DMA ii) Virtual Memory.

subparts.label: a
subparts.text: Write the difference between CISC & RISC Architecture.

subparts.label: b
subparts.text: Write short notes on any one: i) DMA ii) Virtual Memory.

questions.answer:
**a)** CISC has complex multi-cycle instructions, many addressing modes, and microcode; RISC uses a small fixed-length load/store instruction set, many registers, and hardwired pipelining.

**b)** DMA lets an I/O controller transfer blocks directly to/from memory without per-byte CPU intervention; the CPU is interrupted when the transfer completes. Virtual memory maps process virtual addresses to physical frames and swaps pages to secondary storage on demand.

questions.question:
a) What is biased exponent of floating-point number?
b) Discuss in detail the architecture of 8086 microprocessor along with pin configuration diagram.

subparts.label: a
subparts.text: What is biased exponent of floating-point number?

subparts.label: b
subparts.text: Discuss in detail the architecture of 8086 microprocessor along with pin configuration diagram.

questions.answer:
**a)** A bias is added to the true exponent so IEEE-754 exponents are stored as unsigned values (bias 127 for single, 1023 for double).

**b)** 8086 is a 16-bit CPU split into BIU and EU. BIU handles instruction queue, segment registers, and bus; EU has ALU, general registers, flags, and control. It has a 20-bit address bus, 16-bit multiplexed address/data bus, control/status pins, clock, reset, interrupt, and min/max mode pins.

questions.question:
a) Explain the different groups of computers according to Flynn’s classification.
b) Write down the IEEE-754 format for single and double precision numbers.

subparts.label: a
subparts.text: Explain the different groups of computers according to Flynn’s classification.

subparts.label: b
subparts.text: Write down the IEEE-754 format for single and double precision numbers.

questions.answer:
**a)** SISD, SIMD, MISD, MIMD classify machines by number of instruction and data streams.

**b)** Single: 1 sign bit, 8 exponent bits (bias 127), 23 fraction bits. Double: 1 sign bit, 11 exponent bits (bias 1023), 52 fraction bits. Normal values use a hidden leading 1.

questions.question:
a) Describe the concept of Pipeline and its types.
b) Write the different types of pipeline hazards.

subparts.label: a
subparts.text: Describe the concept of Pipeline and its types.

subparts.label: b
subparts.text: Write the different types of pipeline hazards.

questions.answer:
**a)** Pipelining overlaps instruction stages (fetch, decode, execute, memory, write-back). Types include instruction pipelines, arithmetic pipelines, and superscalar/VLIW or superpipelined designs.

**b)** Structural hazards (resource conflicts), data hazards (RAW/WAR/WAW dependencies), and control hazards (branches/interrupts). Forwarding, stalling, branch prediction, and separate caches mitigate them.
